title: Maternal high-fat diet modifies myelin organization, microglial interactions, and results in social memory and sensorimotor gating deficits in adolescent mouse offspring.
ehr_evidence: The study used a maternal high-fat diet (mHFD) mouse model (C57BL/6N mice); data were generated from brain tissue histology, electron microscopy, RT-qPCR, and behavioral assays, not from electronic health records.
summary: In a maternal high-fat diet (mHFD) mouse model, adolescent (P30) offspring of both sexes showed sex-specific myelin changes (reduced cytosolic myelin channels and increased optical density in males), altered microglial phagolysosomal activity and increased synaptic contacts, and behavioral deficits including loss of social novelty preference and reduced prepulse inhibition.
key_findings: Increased myelin optical density in mHFD-exposed male compared to female offspring (male CD vs male mHFD: p = 0.0081, vs female CD: p = 0.0023, vs female mHFD: p = 0.0082)
Reduced area of cytosolic myelin channels in the corpus callosum rostrum of mHFD-exposed male offspring (male CD vs male mHFD: p = 0.0016)
Decreased hippocampal transcripts of Mbp, Cspg4, Olig2, and Igf1 in mHFD-exposed male offspring (Mbp: p = 0.0014 vs male CD; Igf1: p = 0.0412 vs male CD)
No significant change in myelinated axon density, g-ratio, decompacted myelin, or oligodendrocyte density/distribution/maturation
mHFD-exposed microglia showed increased synaptic (pre- and postsynaptic) contacts and reduced mature tertiary lysosomes
Decreased social novelty preference in mHFD-exposed offspring regardless of sex
Reduced prepulse inhibition at the 9 dB prepulse in mHFD-exposed offspring regardless of sex
No significant change in anxiety-related behaviors (open/closed arm time, anxiety index)
captured_features: Cytosolic myelin channel area and ratio
Gene expression (Mbp, Plp1, Cspg4, Olig2, Igf1, Gpnmb) in hippocampus and prefrontal cortex
Microglial density, morphology, lysosome counts, and synaptic contacts
study_design: Controlled experimental animal study (maternal high-fat diet mouse model, diet x sex design)
population: Adolescent C57BL/6N mouse offspring at P30-P40, both sexes
limitations: Mouse model with limited translational relevance to humans
Maternal diet effects on dams not directly quantified in offspring
